bull.t: Near-zero leverage and sizable equity base
bull.b: The sharp reduction in debt materially improves solvency and reduces interest and refinancing pressure compared with 2024. A sizable equity base relative to assets provides financial capacity to support operations and development, although returns remain dependent on achieving commercial scale.

bull.t: Searles Valley adds operating assets and liquidity
bull.b: Completing the Searles Valley acquisition moves the company beyond a purely developmental profile by adding physical production assets and resource access. The stronger asset base and post-closing liquidity can support integration and create a platform for revenue generation over the coming quarters.

bull.t: Integrated U.S. borate platform and resource position
bull.b: The combination of operating infrastructure, long-life brine resources, rail access and established utilities creates a more integrated borate platform. Retaining Fort Cady as a longer-term resource also broadens the company’s potential domestic supply position and product development runway.

bear.t: No revenue and persistent large losses
bear.b: The absence of recorded revenue across multiple annual periods shows that the business has not yet demonstrated commercial scale. Continued material losses, including approximately $43M in 2026, make profitability dependent on successful execution of the newly acquired operating assets.

Recurring negative operating and free cash flow means the company has not been self-funding and must reduce burn or establish revenue to sustain development. Continued cash consumption can constrain investment choices and increase reliance on external capital during the next several quarters.

bear.t: High-cost acquisition financing and covenant constraints
bear.b: The acquisition financing adds substantial obligations before the acquired operations have proven sustainable earnings. High-cost interest, a maturity-linked fee, asset security and covenant restrictions increase financial risk and could limit flexibility if integration or revenue ramp-up takes longer than planned.
